Use this dictionary when a term appears in a workflow or result page. Definitions
follow the current SCGSim contracts; links point to the pages that describe each
workflow in detail.

## Analysis

[Electrostatic]{#term-electrostatic} solves conductor charge for specified
voltages and returns an ordered capacitance matrix. See the
[problem overview](concepts/problems.qmd#capacitance-charge-response-to-conductor-voltage).

[Eigenmode]{#term-eigenmode} finds resonant frequencies and fields for a model
with its declared boundaries and circuit elements. An Eigenmode result and a
driven response are different quantities. See the
[problem overview](concepts/problems.qmd#resonance-modes-of-a-field-and-circuit-model).

[Driven Modal]{#term-driven-modal} is the HFSS driven workflow using modal
ports, including integration-line port declarations, to return complex
S-parameters.

[Driven Terminal]{#term-driven-terminal} is the HFSS driven workflow using
explicit reference conductors to return complex S-parameters.

## Geometry and workflow

[Net]{#term-net} is the caller's electrical grouping of source Entities. It
records connectivity assignments; the geometry API does not infer electrical
connectivity from touching shapes.

[Ground]{#term-ground} is a physical or electrical grounding choice in a
selected model or workflow. It is not synonymous with a particular native
`Net` type; consult the backend contract for how the choice is represented.

[Body]{#term-body} is a geometry object represented in a source or backend
model. Its meaning depends on the geometry contract: a source object may be
interpreted or lowered as a Sheet or Solid, so Body does not by itself mean a
native three-dimensional solid or imply inferred layer spans.

[Occurrence]{#term-occurrence} is a named placement of a component instance in
a hierarchy. Qualified occurrence identity distinguishes repeated instances
while retaining their shared component definition.

[GeometryPlan]{#term-geometry-plan} is the mutable Notebook builder for
component entities and final Net assignments. Calling `prepare()` produces a
detached immutable snapshot.

[Snapshot]{#term-snapshot} is a detached, immutable record of prepared source
geometry and its identities. It carries prepared input without retaining live
component references.

[Mesh]{#term-mesh} is the discretized geometric domain used by a field solver.
A mesh summary describes mesh construction and counts; by itself it does not
establish solver accuracy.

[Adaptive Pass]{#term-adaptive-pass} is a solver's successive mesh/solution
iteration in an adaptive workflow. Interpret values using the actual completed
pass and the backend's recorded history.

[AMR]{#term-amr} means Adaptive Mesh Refinement: the solver refines a mesh
locally or globally during an adaptive workflow, according to its native
procedure.

[Nonconformal AMR]{#term-nonconformal-amr} is Adaptive Mesh Refinement that
allows local refinement to leave neighboring elements at different refinement
levels, creating hanging nodes at nonconforming mesh interfaces. Palace exposes
this as `Model.Refinement.Nonconformal`; see the [MFEM explanation](https://mfem.org/howto/ncmesh/).

[Solver]{#term-solver} is the native computational program that evaluates a
prepared model. SCGSim prepares requests and resolves returned evidence around
the selected solver.

[Handoff]{#term-handoff} is the prepared, identifiable package passed from
model preparation to a caller-controlled solver execution and result return.
It does not itself mean that a solver ran or completed.

## Results

[Sheet]{#term-sheet} is a two-dimensional source or native geometric surface;
it can represent a thin-film region or a port surface depending on its declared
role.

[Solid]{#term-solid} is the volume-based geometry representation selected by
`modeling="solid"`.

[Thin Film]{#term-thin-film} is the explicitly selected thin-film geometry
representation, configured separately from Solid. Its film assumptions and
backend support are documented in the [capability table](backend-support.qmd).

[Port]{#term-port} is a declared excitation or measurement boundary for a
driven calculation. Its type and reference determine how the returned network
response is interpreted.

[Terminal]{#term-terminal} is a conductor endpoint in a terminal formulation.
A terminal's reference conductor is part of the model definition.

[C]{#term-c} denotes capacitance. [G]{#term-g} denotes conductance. [RLGC]{#term-rlgc} means Resistance, Inductance, Conductance, and Capacitance
parameters, often reported per unit length for a cross-section extraction.

[Maxwell capacitance matrix]{#term-maxwell-capacitance-matrix} relates
conductor charges to conductor voltages under the extraction's grounding and
ordering conventions. Preserve its native conductor order and units.

[EPR]{#term-epr} means Energy Participation Ratio: a selected energy numerator
divided by the backend-defined normalization energy. The numerator and
[denominator convention](eigenmode-epr.qmd#quantities-and-normalization) depend
on backend; thin-film estimates contribute numerators and are not added to the
denominator.

[SPR]{#term-spr} means Surface Participation Ratio: estimated energy in a
specified interface film divided by the backend's EPR normalization energy.
It is an interface estimate, not automatically a disjoint part of total energy.

For EPR and SPR, read the numerator and denominator together. They are
dimensionless ratios; do not confuse them with percentages or with loss
contributions such as inverse-Q, which additionally depend on loss assumptions.

[Convergence]{#term-convergence} describes whether a declared quantity
approaches stability under the stated iterative criterion. Record the quantity,
criterion, and stopping reason; interpret native solver flags separately from
any caller-defined measure.

## Symbols and units

Capacitance may be expressed in farads (`F`) or femtofarads (`fF`); `1 fF = 10⁻¹⁵ F`. A ratio is dimensionless, while parts per million (`ppm`) is a scaled
ratio (`1 ppm = 10⁻⁶`). Check the particular API or result contract for its
units; SCGSim APIs do not all use the same unit convention.
